newsitem.title: USA: Stocks drift lower, awaiting outcome of Fed meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stocks drift lower, awaiting outcome of Fed meeting.

text.p: Stock prices drifted lower in cautious trading Tuesday as Wall Street awaited the outcome of a meeting of Federal Reserve policy makers, who were widely expected to hold interest rates steady in their last meeting of the year.
At 1 p.m. EST, the 30-stock Dow Jones index was off 6.54 points at 6,261.81 after rebounding from an early loss of nearly 30 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 13-9 on active volume of 282 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond was off 21/32, raising its yield, which moves in the opposite direction from the price, to 6.68 percent from 6.63 percent at Monday's close.

Stock traders were cautious even though the betting was that the central bank's Federal Open Market Committee would hold interest rates steady. It is expected to announce its decision at about 2:15 p.m. EST (1915 GMT).

"Bonds are dragging stocks lower here," said Henry Herrmann, chief investment officer for Waddell & Reed. "The indexes are performing surprisingly well, but in the underlying broader market, there's not much strength there."
Analysts said bonds fell on news that construction starts on new homes jumped at the fastest rate in more than a year last month, putting builders on track for their best year since 1988.
Total starts increased 9.2 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.514 million in November, the biggest monthly increase since an 11.5 percent surge 16 months earlier in July 1995.

"With the stronger-than-expected numbers, there is some skittishness around. The general consensus is that they will do nothing ... but I'm not sure that even that will give the market a lot of comfort," Herrmann said.
General Electric rose 1-1/8 to 96-3/8 after analysts reported that company Chairman Jack Welch said GE was on track for about 13 percent earnings growth in 1996.

Microsoft Corp. rose 1-5/8 to 78-3/8 and Intel Corp. gained 1-7/16 to 128-3/8, lending some steadiness to the Nasdaq Composite Index after it plunged 24 points Monday in its steepest fall since July 23.
The Nasdaq index was off 4.14 points at 1,256.84. The American Stock Exchange index lost 3.79 to 568.78.
Peggy Farley, chief executive of Amas Securities, said she viewed the drop in technology stocks as a buying opportunity.

"The market is just in the doldrums, because there's not much faith that it will resume upwards. There's a question about what fourth quarter earnings will look like and people are looking further out and wondering about 1997," she said.
Among special situations, Home Depot jumped 1-1/4 to 49-5/8 after Prudential Securities upgraded its opinion of the stock.
Frontier Corp. plunged 6-1/4 to 20-1/8 in heavy trading after the telecommunications holding company warned of weak fourth quarter earnings.
